consumer: The GUI monster-rendering/threat-tint routine that asks 'what color should I draw this visible monster?' and SHOWS that color to the player.
scope: per-visible-monster display attribute (the engine's own threat-to-color mapping for each currently-visible monster); not a possession/mission predicate and not raw world state
decisive_source: The engine's monster threat-coloring routine (e.g. monster::color_with_effects / threat-to-color mapping in the display layer) is NOT shown in the excerpts; the shown excerpts (raw mon.get_hp/hp_max getters, Creature::sees visibility test, avatar scalar getters) are not the decisive authority because they only supply raw state or a see/no-see boolean, not the displayed threat tint.
divergence: A monster whose raw threat scalar maps to one displayed color via the engine's filtered/effect-aware coloring (e.g. it is partially hidden, hallucinated, or under an effect that shifts its on-screen tint) but a re-derivation straight from raw hp/speed picks a different color: the frontend would draw a tint the real GUI never shows, exposing a wrong (D) answer.
